discovery: Proposal and realization of quantum logic with trapped ions, establishing the architecture of the quantum computer

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed, with remarkable conceptual clarity, how a string of laser-cooled ions coupled through their collective motion could perform universal quantum logic. Their proposal was the first physically concrete blueprint of a scalable quantum processor, and it set the language - addressable qubits, a quantum bus, entangling gates - that every hardware platform, including superconducting circuits, later adopted. Blatt turned this blueprint into a working machine: the Innsbruck experiments realized the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement, quantum simulation and elementary error correction with unprecedented fidelity. Together they carried a fundamental idea to the threshold of a technology now pursued by laboratories and companies worldwide. This is precisely the trajectory by which a discovery becomes true: a clean theoretical insight, validated by patient, precise experiments, that enables an entire field.
